summary: The Safer Buildings Coalition opposes conditionally tying E-Rate funding to screen-time limits, arguing that such restrictions could hinder children's access to educational content and learning. The organization highlights the operational reality that Americans spend most of their time indoors and emphasizes the importance of maintaining emergency lifeline connectivity, including 911 access and parent contact, which may be compromised by screen-time restrictions. The organization also notes the  The School Mode framework proposes a balanced approach to screen-time management for E-Rate-funded services, aiming to reduce distractions while preserving critical emergency communication capabilities. The comment supports preserving emergency communication capabilities under CIPA restrictions, recognizing the importance of maintaining access to 911, parent contact, and IPAWS-triggered alerts while considering device-level restrictions. Stakeholders support restricting phone use during class time but not all day. Parents are excluded from policy decisions. In-building wireless reliability during emergencies is insufficiently addressed. Policies requiring phone storage eliminate backup communication channels during emergencies. E-Rate eligibility should not condition on screen-time limits
